text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
OrdersTakeoutFrequent(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah(x) ::: x is Hannah.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people work in student jobs, they need to earn money.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequent(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequent(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, they spend a lot of time eating and catching up.

Hannah(AtSchoolHannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(AtSchoolHannah) ::: Hannah works in student jobs on campus.
∀x (NeedsMoney(x) → (¬PickyEater(x) ∧ NeedsMoney(x))) ::: If she needs to earn money, then she is not a picky eater and she needs to earn money.

Conclusion:
AtSchoolHannah ∧ (¬PickyEater(AtSchoolHannah) ∨ (PickyEater(AtSchoolHannah) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(AtSchoolHannah))) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and she either is not a picky eater or, if she is, then she spends a lot of her time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
